stem: The points $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ lie on a circle, in this order around the circle. Draw the chords $AC$, $BD$, $AD$ and $CD$. Given that $m(\angle ABD) = {=q}^\circ$ and $m(\angle CBD) = {=p}^\circ$, find $m(\angle ADC)$ in degrees.
solution: $\angle CAD$ and $\angle CBD$ are inscribed angles including the same arc $CD$, so $m(\angle CAD) = m(\angle CBD) = {=p}^\circ$.
$\angle ACD$ and $\angle ABD$ are inscribed angles including the same arc $AD$, so $m(\angle ACD) = m(\angle ABD) = {=q}^\circ$.
notes: Text-only two-step: same-arc equality twice, then triangle angle sum (as in book drill 1-3). Order A,B,C,D on circle makes B and A on the same side of CD, and B and C on the same side of AD, so the equalities hold. Any p+q<180 is geometrically valid.
